title: Anatomical position and directions
summary: Compare anatomical left and right, and proximal, distal, medial and lateral positions.
task: Identify the radius on the thumb side and the ulna on the little-finger side in anatomical position.

title: Axial skeleton and landmarks
summary: Examine the skull, breastbone and first two cervical vertebrae.
task: Use posterior and lateral views to distinguish C1 from C2 and the manubrium from the body of the sternum.

title: Appendicular skeleton
summary: Trace the pectoral girdle and upper and lower limb bones.
task: Pull the femur away and examine its relationship to the pelvis and tibia.

title: Shoulder and rotator cuff
summary: Find the actual deltoid portions and rotator cuff muscles in the 3D atlas.
task: Pull the superficial deltoid portions aside to study the deeper rotator cuff.

title: Peripheral nerves
summary: Identify major upper and lower limb peripheral nerves.
task: Follow the course of each nerve and compare its relationship with nearby bones and muscles.

title: Respiratory and digestive organs
summary: Identify the precise pulmonary lobes and other visceral structures present in the atlas.
task: Remove pulmonary lobes one at a time to view the trachea and underlying upper abdominal organs.

title: Cardiac chambers
summary: Explore the heart using the chambers available in the atlas's cardiovascular system.
task: Isolate each cardiac chamber and rotate the model to understand the relationship between atria and ventricles.
